I found no direct empirical validation that measured easy-negative gradient saturation predicts subsequent semi-hard-sampling gains beyond training margins and candidate ranks. [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.07192) establishes a different mechanism: sampled BCE produces overconfident probabilities; increasing uniformly sampled negatives and changing calibration through gBCE improves held-out ranking. Its loss-by-negative-count ablations support those interventions, not saturation as a predictor of semi-hard sampling benefit. [SRNS](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2020/hash/0c7119e3a6a2209da6a5b90e5b5b75bd-Abstract.html) provides closer evidence: few negatives are informative, false negatives often have stable predictions, and variance-aware sampling improves robustness on synthetic and real datasets. Neither establishes the requested incremental diagnostic relationship.

[Evaluating Performance and Bias of Negative Sampling](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.17276v1) compares six samplers with hyperparameter optimization and 20 repeats across three datasets. Uniform sampling favors head items; popularity-based sampling can improve balance while reducing aggregate accuracy. Evaluation ranks the full catalog, so its findings do not directly establish gains under fixed 99-negative HR@10. Excluding observed history also cannot certify that remaining items are true negatives. The study compares sampler outcomes rather than testing whether saturation forecasts their gains.

Practical inference: treat saturation as a hypothesis generator. For BPR, the score-gradient magnitude is sigmoid(negative score − positive score), so it largely restates the margin; BCE negative gradients similarly restate negative logits. Measurements on already fitted training examples can therefore indicate memorization without establishing generalization. Test added value through matched uniform-versus-semi-hard NextItNet runs, controlling negative count, compute, loss, history exclusions and popularity composition; retain one model per category. Judge gains using the pinned validation users/candidates and macro HR@10, without consulting hidden test labels.
